edits.before: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional complex representation and $r$ an element of finite order $m$. On $V\lambda$ every power $r^{k}$ acts by $\lambda ^{k}$; its dimension is the multiplicity of that one-dimensional cyclic representation. In the natural three-dimensional cube representation, a quarter-turn about the vertical axis has eigenvalues 1, $i$ and $-i$. The real horizontal plane splits into two lines only after complexification.
